description: Converts geometry between Tekla Structures 2020 and GeometryHelper: points, vectors, segments, planes, coordinate systems, bounding boxes, transformation matrices, and the faces and loops of a Tekla solid. Also reads the objects of IFC reference models into solids placed where Tekla shows them, through GeometryHelper.IfcConvert. Built for Tekla Structures 2020; install the package whose year matches your Tekla.
releaseNotes:
NEW IN 11.2.0
      - GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert is released at 11.2.0 with GeometryHelper, whose GeoSolid3.TrySubtractAll, given
        SolidClosingOptions, closes a cut it would otherwise skip: of the 79 864 parts of a Tekla model, 17 had 35 cuts
        skipped; closing takes 9 and leaves 10, and the 8 whose cuts within a hundredth are valid come out within 0.12 %
        of those, where skipping left them up to 10 % off.

      NEW IN 11.1.0
      - GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert is released at 11.1.0 with GeometryHelper, which adds GeoSolid3.TryClose: a body read
        open is closed with the least change that does it, with a report of what it changed, or of why it would not. Of
        the 35 cuts GeoSolid3.TrySubtractAll skips on the 79 864 parts of a Tekla model, 23 close within a gap of 0.005,
        none further from the same cut within a hundredth than 2.1 parts in a million.

      NEW IN 11.0.1
      - GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert is released at 11.0.1 with GeometryHelper, whose GeoSolid3.TrySubtractAll with a
        contact and a fallback of a hundredth takes a part's net body as before, more of its cuts closed: of 79 864 parts
        of a Tekla model, 17 have a cut skipped where 19 had, and none comes out more than a litre from the same cuts
        within a hundredth, where two did.

      NEW IN 11.0.0
      - GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert is released at 11.0.0 with GeometryHelper, whose default tolerance is a thousandth
        of a millimetre now, where it was a hundredth: this BREAKS code that relied on points 0.001 to 0.01 apart being
        one. Read within the default, the 79 864 parts of a Tekla model came out closed; a face further out of flat than
        a thousandth comes as triangles on its own corners.
      - For a part's net body, GeoSolid3.TrySubtractAll with SolidBooleanOptions, a Contact of a hundredth and a Fallback
        of a hundredth: Tekla Structures draws parts a few thousandths into or off each other, and within a thousandth
        alone a part keeps a skin of itself where a cutter's face stood that far inside its own.

      NEW IN 10.0.0
      - GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert reads as before: it is released at 10.0.0 with GeometryHelper, which BREAKS code
        that measures a body: GeoSolid3.Volume, SurfaceArea and Centroid are GetVolume(), GetSurfaceArea() and
        GetCentroid() now, the material of a body with its openings cut out. A body TryToGeoSolid3 reads has its cuts in
        its faces and no openings, so it measures as before: a slab cut by five other parts matched VOLUME_NET and AREA
        to 5E-12.
      - GeometryHelper's booleans no longer lose the wedge two slabs share where one wraps the other's corner at a
        slant: 15.79 million cubic millimetres, of which the difference took none.

      NEW IN 9.0.2
      - Nothing in GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert itself changed: it is released at 9.0.2 with GeometryHelper, which
        meshes the faces of bodies read with TryToGeoSolid3 round every hole, a slab's pits among them, where it laid
        the fan of a face's boundary across them.

      NEW IN 9.0.1
      - Nothing in GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert itself changed: it is released at 9.0.1 with GeometryHelper, whose
        solid booleans no longer take material from a body another only touches, the way slabs read with
        TryToGeoSolid3 meet, nor give it back larger than it was.

      NEW IN 9.0.0
      - BREAKING: FaceConvert.TryReadFace and LoopConvert.TryReadLoop are removed; read a Tekla face with
        FaceConvert.TryReadFaces. Each read one face, or one polygon, or nothing: a face out of flat came back as
        nothing and a hole off its plane was dropped, so a body put together from them was open where Tekla holds it
        closed. TryReadFaces gives the triangles on the face's own corners instead, and TryToGeoSolid3 reads with it.

      NEW IN 8.0.0
      - TryToGeoSolid3 reads each face with the new FaceConvert.TryReadFaces: a face out of flat, or with a hole off
        its plane, comes as triangles on the corners Tekla gave, where it was refused or lost its hole and left the
        body open. A solid Tekla holds closed comes out closed whatever the tolerance. TryReadFace reads as before.
      - From GeometryHelper 8.0.0: the default tolerance is a hundredth of a millimetre for points and for flatness.
      - Reference models read as GeometryHelper.IfcConvert 8.0.0 reads them.

      NEW IN 7.0.0
      - Nothing in GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert changed: it is released at 7.0.0 with GeometryHelper, whose label
        placement changed in ways that break code reading ArrangeItem.Offset.

      NEW IN 6.3.0
      - Nothing in GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert changed: it is released at 6.3.0 with GeometryHelper, whose label
        placement takes a gap of its own for each side of a leader.

      NEW IN 6.2.0
      - A reference model read whole (ReferenceModelConvert.ToGeoSolids / ToIfcGeometries) is converted and
        carried into the work plane on every core at once: three Tekla reference models of about 21,000
        products each came back in 28 s instead of 85 s, the bodies the same. The bodies of one brep come back
        in one order (GeometryHelper.IfcConvert).

      Converts geometry between Tekla Structures and GeometryHelper, both ways: points, vectors, line
      segments, geometric planes, coordinate systems, bounding boxes, transformation matrices, and the
      faces and loops of a Tekla solid.

      BUILT FOR TEKLA STRUCTURES 2020
      - This package references the Tekla Structures 2020 Open API. Tekla's assemblies are
        strong-named per release and a plugin cannot redirect between them, so install the package whose
        year matches your Tekla: GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2020, GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2025 or
        GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2026. It replaces the former GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert package, which
        was built against 2020 only.

      REQUIRES THREE ASSEMBLIES YOU MUST SUPPLY
      - Tekla.Structures.dll, Tekla.Structures.Drawing.dll and Tekla.Structures.Model.dll are not
        redistributed here, because they are Trimble's to ship rather than ours. Reference them yourself,
        either from the bin folder of your Tekla Structures installation or from Trimble's own
        Tekla.Structures, Tekla.Structures.Drawing and Tekla.Structures.Model packages on nuget.org.
        Without them the compiler reports CS0012.

      IFC REFERENCE MODELS
      - ReferenceModelObjectConvert.ToGeoSolids / ToIfcGeometries read the selected objects of IFC
        reference models, and ReferenceModelConvert.ToGeoSolids / ToIfcGeometries every physical product
        of a reference model, in the current work plane: the IFC file is read in millimetres at the
        reference model's scale and placed where the reference model was inserted.
      - ToIfcGeometries returns each IFC product whole (IfcProductGeometry): bodies, open surfaces,
        placement, GlobalId, name, type and conversion warnings.
      - Bolts make a whole Tekla model slow to read. IfcConvertOptions.SkipNames and OnlyNames choose the
        products by name before any geometry is built: a 115 MB steel model read in 35 s without its bolts
        and in 3.5 s for its main members, against about 17 minutes for every product.
      - Reference models that are not IFC, files that cannot be read and objects that cannot be converted
        are left out rather than thrown on, and written to GeometryHelperLog (GeometryHelper).
        Each IFC file is parsed once per process and then cached.
      - The objects of a file read into memory are converted on every core at once and come back in the
        order asked for, and geometry that products share is built once (GeometryHelper.IfcConvert):
        2,549 objects selected in Tekla from one 6.8 MB ifczip came back in 4.9 s instead of 84 s, the
        bodies byte for byte the same. A large file xBIM keeps on disk is still read one object at a time.
        Every object is converted under the tolerance in force where the method is called, a
        Tolerance.Use scope included.
      - So is every product of a reference model read whole (ReferenceModelConvert.ToGeoSolids /
        ToIfcGeometries), and each is carried into the work plane on every core at once too: three
        reference models of about 21,000 products each, read whole outside Tekla on 24 logical processors,
        came back in 28 s instead of 85 s, and in 14 s instead of 80 s with the server garbage collector,
        the bodies the same.
      - These read IFC through GeometryHelper.IfcConvert, which this package depends on. They run on
        .NET Framework 4.8 x64, and Xbim.Geometry.Engine64.dll, which the build copies next to your
        plugin, has to ship with it.

      DRAWING IN THE MODEL VIEW
      - GeometryDraw.DrawToTekla draws polylines, polygons, faces and solids (and DrawPolyline points) as
        control polycurves in the current work plane. Faces are drawn with their outer boundary in red and
        their holes in white unless other colours are passed. An arc or a circle draws as well, cut into
        straight pieces within 0.2 % of its radius, which is finer than a model view resolves. The polycurves are returned so that Delete()
        can take them away again. Call Model.CommitChanges() afterwards; the methods do not commit.

      READING A SOLID
      - Faces are turned to agree with the normal Tekla gives them, and the body is turned inside out
        if its signed volume says the whole surface arrived reversed. A coordinate system whose Y axis
        is not quite square to its X axis is squared up rather than trusted.
      - A face that cannot be made sense of is skipped rather than thrown on, which leaves the body no
        longer closed, so ask IsClosed() before trusting a volume.
      - Tekla models in millimetres with coordinates running to hundreds of thousands, where the
        default EqualPlanar is often too tight. Pass a Tolerance suited to the model.
